scope: All 18 frozen evidence entries in CORE-01–CORE-03; no source or pack modifications
method: Exact frozen claims mechanically compared with masked packets; cited external text inspected; historical support is separate from cutoff availability and model confidence. No blanket confidence upgrades. Source reconstruction dates do not themselves make earlier facts inadmissible.

sources.title: CDC, The Untreated Syphilis Study at Tuskegee Timeline
sources.limits: Modern retrospective page; not the document available to a 1969 panel.

sources.title: CDC, About The Untreated Syphilis Study at Tuskegee
sources.limits: Confirms broad historical facts, not individual clinical status in February 1969.

sources.title: CDC Museum, Public Health Service Study of Untreated Syphilis at Tuskegee and Macon County
sources.limits: Short history records questions in 1968; original objection correspondence not inspected.

sources.title: Martin J. Tobin, Fiftieth Anniversary of Uncovering the Tuskegee Syphilis Study
sources.limits: Not used as claim support. Manifest gives 2023, but PubMed identifies 2022 publication.

sources.locator: Citation: Am J Respir Crit Care Med 205(10):1145–1158; DOI 10.1164/rccm.202201-0136SO
sources.limits: Used only to correct publication date; abstract does not replace full-text verification.

sources.title: Final Report of the Tuskegee Syphilis Study Ad Hoc Advisory Panel
sources.source_kind: primary official investigation; later reconstruction and reproduced earlier records
sources.locator: Printed pp. 7–16, 18 and 31; reproduced February 6, 1969 summary at printed pp. 10–11
sources.limits: CDC links this hosted copy. February 1969 summary is reproduced retrospectively; 1970 memoranda and 1973 judgments must remain outside the cutoff.

sources.title: A. J. McDonald account of January 27, reproduced in Rogers Commission hearings
sources.source_kind: primary witness account with notes and later addendum
sources.locator: Volume IV pp. 740–746; numbered note pages 1–14
sources.limits: Title describes January 27 events, but document includes February 13 addendum. Do not label the entire text as demonstrably contemporaneous transcription.

sources.title: Rogers Commission, Volume I Chapter V
sources.locator: Launch-decision testimony and timeline, printed pp. 108–109
sources.limits: Supports reconstructed pre-decision sequence; post-recommendation events and accident findings excluded from evaluator evidence.

sources.title: FDA historical exhibit: Frances Oldham Kelsey
sources.locator: Paragraphs beginning Six years later and The company continued
sources.limits: High-level narrative, not a dated 1960–61 NDA dossier; cannot establish every negative claim about available adverse-event evidence.

sources.title: FDA, The History of Drug Regulation in the United States, Centennial Edition
sources.locator: PDF page 6 (one-based), printed page 8, Drug Efficacy—1962 material
sources.limits: Manifest calls this a historical exhibit; actual PDF is the 2006 booklet. Outcome material is excluded from cutoff evidence.

sources.title: FDA, A Brief History of CDER
sources.locator: Frances Kelsey, Thalidomide, and a Global Disaster Narrowly Averted Here
sources.limits: Establishes broad chronology, not a precise last pre-discovery review date.

claims.claim: The programme began decades earlier to observe the natural history of the infection and includes an infected group and a control group.
claims.support: CDC records the 1932 observational study and separate infected and uninfected cohorts.
claims.decision_time_assessment: Study design predates February 1969 and would be institutionally available; audited source is retrospective.
claims.epistemic_status_assessment: Observed is reasonable for documented design, not direct observation by this auditor.
claims.masked_fidelity: Faithful identity removal; infected/control structure retained.
claims.correction_or_recommendation: Attach source and locator. Keep evidence of study design separate from judgments about its worth.

claims.claim: Participants were not given informed consent to an untreated-disease experiment and were led to believe they were receiving health care for a broad illness description.

sources.locator: FAQ: Why was the study unethical?

claims.support: CDC describes missing informed consent and misleading presentation as treatment.
claims.decision_time_assessment: Underlying conduct occurred before cutoff; retrospective finding does not prove every panel member knew every detail.
claims.epistemic_status_assessment: Observed should be understood as documented historical conduct; no interview-level consent record inspected.
claims.masked_fidelity: Faithful; broad illness description preserves deception while suppressing identifying phrase.
claims.correction_or_recommendation: Record historical support separately from evidence of what each decision-maker knew.

claims.claim: A highly effective treatment has been the accepted treatment of choice and widely available for many years, but participants have not routinely been offered it by the study.

sources.locator: Printed pp. 9–11: Facts and Documentation re Charge I-B

claims.support: Penicillin availability and non-offering are documented; individual histories and clinical suitability varied.
claims.decision_time_assessment: Treatment knowledge predates 1969. The 1973 review cites earlier treatment literature, but is not itself cutoff evidence.
claims.epistemic_status_assessment: Observed broadly supported; highly effective does not mean a guaranteed cure for every survivor.
claims.masked_fidelity: Broadly faithful; omitted transparent uncertainty about each survivor’s health and treatment history matters.
claims.correction_or_recommendation: Restore patient-specific clinical uncertainty in a candidate packet; distinguish offering assessment/treatment from forced uniform therapy.

claims.claim: An internal adviser has raised ethical objections and asked leadership to reconsider continuation.
claims.support: CDC identifies internal questioning by its public-health adviser in 1968.
claims.decision_time_assessment: Objection precedes February 1969; original letters and precise recipients were not inspected.
claims.epistemic_status_assessment: Reported is appropriate. Exact wording of a request to leadership remains less directly evidenced.
claims.correction_or_recommendation: Attach the retrospective source now; obtain original correspondence before asserting exact notice to named decision-makers.

claims.claim: Supporters of continuation argue that the long longitudinal dataset is scientifically unique and cannot be recreated if treatment changes the course of disease.

sources.locator: Printed pp. 10–11, reproduced February 6, 1969 meeting summary

claims.support: The summary cites remaining research value and nonrepeatability, without the exact treatment-counterfactual rationale.
claims.decision_time_assessment: Reproduced 1969 meeting material is temporally relevant; the 1970 value criticism must not be imported.
claims.epistemic_status_assessment: Reported is appropriate for proponents’ rationale. The precise causal embellishment lacks direct support inspected here.
claims.masked_fidelity: Masked cannot be recreated is stronger than transparent cannot readily be recreated.
claims.correction_or_recommendation: Replace with the narrower documented continuation rationale; label any treatment-counterfactual conclusion as inference.

claims.claim: The untreated infection can cause severe illness, death and transmission; the incremental scientific value of further untreated observation is uncertain.

sources.locator: Printed pp. 7, 9 and 18: risk, treatment history and background

claims.support: Historical disease risks are documented. The compound claim’s marginal-value uncertainty is an analytical characterization.
claims.decision_time_assessment: General risks predate cutoff; do not treat later value judgments or all-stage transmission as proven for each 1969 survivor.
claims.epistemic_status_assessment: Split observed general disease hazards from inferred/uncertain incremental research value.
claims.masked_fidelity: Faithful to the transparent compound claim, but both compress distinct epistemic categories.
claims.correction_or_recommendation: Split into atomic claims; qualify stage-specific transmission and individual risk; retain marginal value as an explicit uncertainty.

claims.claim: Forecast conditions are substantially colder than any prior comparable successful operational mission.
claims.support: Forecast conditions fell below the prior flight temperature used in the engineering recommendation.
claims.decision_time_assessment: Forecast was circulated before the final recommendation.
claims.epistemic_status_assessment: Predicted is correct; distinguish ambient forecast from calculated seal temperature.
claims.masked_fidelity: Faithful relative comparison; exact identifying temperatures removed.
claims.correction_or_recommendation: Maintain the distinction between environmental forecast and component temperature.

claims.claim: Engineering analysis says colder conditions slow a critical joint seal's response and recommends not operating outside the coldest demonstrated flight experience.
claims.support: Presented charts connected colder conditions with slower sealing and supported the initial no-launch advice.
claims.decision_time_assessment: Discussed before the managerial caucus and recommendation.
claims.epistemic_status_assessment: Reported engineering analysis is correctly distinguished from a quantified failure probability.
claims.correction_or_recommendation: Attach the contemporaneous-event witness account, with its retrospective-document qualification.

claims.claim: The coldest prior comparable mission showed the most severe observed evidence of gas passing the primary seal.
claims.support: Prior coldest flight had the most pronounced primary-seal bypass evidence in the presented comparison.
claims.decision_time_assessment: Prior flight observations were presented before the decision.
claims.epistemic_status_assessment: Observed applies to prior inspection findings, not the future launch outcome.
claims.masked_fidelity: Faithful; bypass does not necessarily mean total joint failure.
claims.correction_or_recommendation: Avoid converting this ordinal comparison into a numerical failure-rate estimate.

claims.claim: Management challenges a simple temperature correlation because a warmer mission also showed some seal bypass and a colder ground test did not show the same problem; engineers dispute whether the ground test is representative of flight conditions.
claims.support: Warmer-flight and ground-test counterexamples were discussed; test preparation limited comparability.
claims.decision_time_assessment: Counterarguments and representativeness objection appear before the caucus.
claims.epistemic_status_assessment: Disputed is apt for representativeness; existence of cited observations is separately documented.
claims.masked_fidelity: Faithful; retains counterevidence absent in a simplistic catastrophe narrative.
claims.correction_or_recommendation: Preserve the counterevidence and split observation from disputed interpretation if atomizing claims.

claims.claim: The dataset is limited and does not establish a precise probability of failure at the forecast conditions.

sources.locator: Timeline at approximately 11:00 p.m.; printed pp. 108–109

claims.support: The record describes inconclusive temperature evidence; no precise probability is established by the cited discussion.
claims.decision_time_assessment: Limited evidence is pre-decision; explicit later complaint about an exact threshold must not supply earlier knowledge.
claims.epistemic_status_assessment: Inference/uncertainty fits better than observed for a negative statistical-sufficiency claim.
claims.masked_fidelity: Masked text substitutes lack of precise probability for the transparent claim about participants’ disagreement.
claims.correction_or_recommendation: Retain as a clearly labelled audit inference or restore the documented discussion; distinguish temperature threshold from probability.

claims.claim: Programme managers note that accepting the proposed environmental limit would disrupt the current mission and constrain future schedule targets.
claims.support: Managers raised current-launch delay and future launch-rate implications of the proposed limit.
claims.decision_time_assessment: Recorded before reassessment and final recommendation.
claims.epistemic_status_assessment: Reported is appropriate; no inference about secret motive is required.
claims.correction_or_recommendation: Attach locator; separate operational consequences from evidence about physical safety.

claims.claim: A senior contractor representative remains uncomfortable with approval, argues that colder conditions move sealing performance in the wrong direction, and proposes waiting for less extreme conditions.

sources.locator: Timeline 10:30–11:00 p.m. and 11:15–11:30 p.m.; printed pp. 108–109

claims.support: Objection and delay proposal precede recommendation; the explicit discomfort statement follows it.
claims.decision_time_assessment: Compound claim crosses the manifest cutoff before final recommendation. Earlier dissent is admissible; later reaction is not.
claims.epistemic_status_assessment: Reported is appropriate only after separating the two moments.
claims.masked_fidelity: Faithful to transparent text, so the timing problem originates in both packets.
claims.correction_or_recommendation: Candidate wording should retain only pre-recommendation dissent/delay; retain later discomfort in the outcome/reconstruction record.

claims.claim: The medicine is already available in many foreign markets.
claims.support: FDA identifies widespread foreign marketing before the domestic application review.
claims.decision_time_assessment: Existing marketing predates the review; support is retrospective institutional history.
claims.epistemic_status_assessment: Observed is reasonable for marketing status, not evidence of adequate safety surveillance.
claims.masked_fidelity: Faithful: many replaces dozens without changing the central comparison.
claims.correction_or_recommendation: Attach source and avoid treating sales as proof of safety.

claims.claim: The regulatory system requires evidence supporting safety before broad domestic marketing.
claims.support: FDA describes a premarketing manufacturer duty to provide safety evidence.
claims.decision_time_assessment: Historical duty applies during the review; not a claim about today’s regulation.
claims.epistemic_status_assessment: Observed describes the historical regulatory framework; original statute was not independently inspected.
claims.masked_fidelity: Faithful summary; omits legal mechanics of an application becoming effective.
claims.correction_or_recommendation: Keep as historical framework; cite contemporaneous statute if more exact procedural claims are added.

claims.claim: The medical reviewer considers the present safety evidence inadequate/incomplete and requests scientifically reliable evidence addressing the deficiencies.

sources.locator: Paragraphs beginning Six years later and The company continued
PDF p. 6, printed p. 8, paragraphs on September 12, 1960 NDA

claims.support: FDA attributes continued deferral to inadequate safety evidence and requests for reliable substantiation.
claims.decision_time_assessment: Relevant during 1960–61, but a single dated review event has not been fixed.
claims.epistemic_status_assessment: Observed establishes the reviewer’s position, not an independent claim-by-claim assessment of the missing dossier.
claims.correction_or_recommendation: Specify a single review date and the material deficiencies before a more detailed evidence challenge.

claims.claim: The manufacturer disputes the need for continued delay and repeatedly supplies material it says demonstrates safety.
claims.support: The historical account records repeated submissions and company pressure while review continued.
claims.decision_time_assessment: Occurred during the review; exact exchanges need dating for a point-in-time packet.
claims.epistemic_status_assessment: Reported appropriately attributes the claimed proof to the applicant.
claims.correction_or_recommendation: Retain attribution; do not imply the applicant’s proof claim was scientifically established.

claims.claim: No specific catastrophic adverse effect is established in the evidence available for this decision; the risk question is genuinely uncertain.
claims.support: FDA places recognition of the birth-defect association in late 1961; this does not establish absence of every serious adverse signal.
claims.decision_time_assessment: Cutoff spans many review events. Before November withdrawal is not equivalent to before association became known.
claims.epistemic_status_assessment: An absence-of-evidence statement and packet boundary are not an observed clinical fact.
claims.masked_fidelity: Material broadening: transparent text excludes later congenital-risk evidence from this packet; masked text generalizes to any specific catastrophe.
claims.correction_or_recommendation: Pin the cutoff to a dated pre-discovery review; state narrowly what this packet establishes, and audit known adverse signals for that date.

cross_case_findings.finding: CORE-01 E5 overstates nonrepeatability and adds an unverified treatment counterfactual.
cross_case_findings.recommendation: Narrow to the documented 1969 research-value rationale.

cross_case_findings.finding: CORE-01 E6 merges general disease risks with uncertain marginal scientific value.
cross_case_findings.recommendation: Separate epistemic classes and qualify stage-specific risks.

cross_case_findings.finding: CORE-02 E7 includes an explicit post-recommendation reaction.
cross_case_findings.recommendation: Retain only prior dissent for the manifest cutoff.

cross_case_findings.finding: CORE-02 source combines event notes with a later addendum, and E5 changes the transparent epistemic proposition.
cross_case_findings.recommendation: Qualify the source temporal role and label the statistical-sufficiency inference.

cross_case_findings.finding: CORE-03 E5 materially broadens the transparent packet and the cutoff covers changing evidence.
cross_case_findings.recommendation: Restore the narrow packet-boundary claim and choose a dated decision event.

cross_case_findings.finding: Tuskegee review source date is 2022, not the manifest’s 2023; its full text was inaccessible.
cross_case_findings.recommendation: Correct bibliography in a candidate revision; rely on inspected primary report for supported claims.
